--- Fonts.md ---
Editor font size
SilverBullet uses three fonts, each picked separately in [[Workbench/Configuration]] under **Appearance**:

* **Interface font**: menus, panels, the page title and the [[Workbench]].
* **Editor font**: the text of your pages.
* **Code font**: anything code-like: inline code, [[Markdown/Fenced Code Block|code blocks]], frontmatter and tables while you edit them, and `${...}` expressions while the cursor is in them. It should be a monospace font.

Instead of using the [[Workbench/Configuration]] options, you can also set them in [[CONFIG]]:

```lua
config.set("fonts.editor", "inter")
config.set("fonts.ui", "system-sans")
config.set("fonts.code", "ia-writer-mono")
```

--- Fonts.md ---
Editor font size | The default font
When a space doesn’t pick an interface or editor font, it uses the default font: in SilverBullet Server, the **Default font** in the dashboard's Server settings; in SilverBullet Desktop, **Font** under Advanced. The default font also sets the dashboard and sign-in pages.

--- Fonts.md ---
Editor font size | Notes for theme authors
If your [[Space Style]] sets fonts, a few things changed with this feature:

* **Code no longer follows `--editor-font`.** It uses `--editor-monospace-font`. A theme that set `--editor-font` to a monospace font, and expected code to follow, should set `--editor-monospace-font` too.
* **The editor's text size is the `--editor-font-size` variable** (18px in the theme), no longer a fixed `font-size` on `#sb-main .cm-editor`.
* **A `space-style` that sets `--editor-font`, `--ui-font`, `--editor-monospace-font` or `--editor-font-size` wins over the Configuration setting**, whether it sets them on `html` or `:root`. Remove it from your style to pick fonts in Configuration instead.
* **Numbered lists right-align their numbers** to the widest number in the list, so items `9.` and `10.` start their text in the same place.

--- Guide/Make it your own.md ---
Get comfortable | Get comfortable
Open any page with some text, then press **Cmd-,** on macOS or **Ctrl-,** on Windows/Linux to open Configuration in [[Workbench]]. You can also open the command palette with **Cmd-/** or **Ctrl-/** and run **Workbench: Configuration**.

Choose **Appearance** in the sidebar. Experiment with the font options (the changes should apply instantly) and once you’re happy, click **Save and apply**.

![Configuration’s Appearance controls with Inter selected as the editor font and the font size set to 20.](../Screenshots/customization-appearance.png)
The interface, page text and code each have their own font setting. Try the built-in choices to find what suits you. [[Fonts]] explains the choices.

To undo a saved setting, open its ⋯ menu, choose **Reset to default**, then **Save and apply** again.

--- CHANGELOG.md ---
CHANGELOG | Edge
* Related Pages and [[Linked Mention|Linked Mentions]] show compact, formatted excerpts with clickable links. Space Lua widgets can use the same renderer through `widget.markdownSummary` (see [[API/widget]]).
* [[Live Object Edit]]: form-based editing for [[Frontmatter]] and [[Tag/data]] objects.
* [[Fonts]]: pick the interface, editor and code fonts in [[Workbench/Configuration]] (Appearance), **including proportional** ones, and the editor's text size. A server-wide **Default font** (Dashboard → Server) sets the dashboard and every space that doesn’t pick its own.
  * **Potentially breaking for themes:** code (inline and fenced, frontmatter, tables being edited, `${...}`) now uses `--editor-monospace-font` instead of `--editor-font`. See [[Fonts#Notes for theme authors]].
